plan:
COMPLETE EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed; no simulated results)

# 0 Scope
Single research question: "Does BAdam produce a learning perturbation with heavy-tailed singular value distribution and effective rank comparable to Adam across transformer modules during finetuning?" Answer via a fully paired, controlled, pre-registered experiment. Only the optimizer structure differs between arms; model, initialization, data, schedule, and evaluation are held fixed.

# 1 Model, dataset, modules

1.1 Model (concrete, unique, CPU-feasible): a small LLaMA-style decoder-only transformer ("tiny-llama-110M" style):
- d_model=768, n_layers=12, n_heads=12, head_dim=64, intermediate_size=2048, vocab_size=32000, seq_len=256, max_pos=512, RoPE rotary, RMSNorm (no bias anywhere — LLaMA convention), SwiGLU gated MLP (up/gate/down), tie_word_embeddings=True, final causal-LM head reuses the embedding.
- Parameter estimate: embedding 32000×768 ≈ 24.6M; per layer: q,k,v,o each 768×768 (0.59M×4), up/gate 768×2048 (1.57M×2), down 2048×768 (1.57M) → ≈7.08M; ×12 ≈ 85M; total ≈ 24.6 + 85 ≈ 110M (weight-tying removes the separate lm_head). Within the ~60–125M budget.
- Justification for decoder (not BERT-style encoder): (a) BAdam was introduced and evaluated on decoder-only LLM finetuning (LLaMA-2-7B on instruction/GSM8K data), so a LLaMA-style decoder is the faithful scale-down analog; (b) it naturally provides all 7 named dense 2D modules and a clean gated-MLP decomposition; (c) causal LM finetuning is a single, unambiguous supervised objective with a stable loss; and (d) LLaMA has no bias/LN weight matrices to accidentally include, so the module set is exactly the dense 2D matrices.

1.2 Analyzed modules (primary set): per layer ℓ ∈ {0..11}: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj (768×768), up_proj (768×2048), gate_proj (768×2048), down_proj (2048×768) → 7 matrices/layer × 12 layers = 84 matrix-modules analyzed.
- Explicitly EXCLUDED from the primary analysis: token embedding and lm_head (large narrow-vocab 2D but qualitatively different + tied, analyzed in appendix only), RMSNorm (1D diag), any bias (none exist by construction), attention masks/scales (not weights).
- For each module we SVD the 2D perturbation matrix ΔW_m (see 2.1); all analyzed matrices are 2D so the SVD and all spectral descriptors are well-defined.

1.3 Dataset/task: fine-grained finetuning = next-token prediction on a fixed, locally stored 1,000,000-token contiguous slice of an open text corpus (Wikitext-2 or an OpenWebText-style slice; tokenized once with the same tokenizer). Steps per epoch = 1e6 / (16 batch × 256 seq) ≈ 244; primary protocol = 3 epochs → T = 733 optimizer steps. Validation = held-out 5k-token slice, same for every arm. (In this sandbox no dataset download is possible; the design assumes a local file is provided in a real run.)

# 2 Core measure definitions and pre-registered decision rule

2.1 Learning perturbation per module m: ΔW_m = W_T^m − W_0^m (final applied accumulated update). This equals the sum of per-step applied updates because at each step the parameter changes exactly by the applied optimizer increment (Adam or block-Adam on active block steps; frozen blocks get zero increments). Record additionally, per module: number of active (nonzero-gradient/solver) steps n_m and the Frobenius norm ‖ΔW_m‖_F (scale diagnostic; all shape metrics below are scale-invariant by construction, so the expected BAdam/Adam magnitude difference does not drive the verdict).

2.2 Heavy-tailed singular value measures (over sorted singular values s_1 ≥ s_2 ≥ … ≥ s_d of ΔW_m):
- PRIMARY tail index α_P: Clauset–Shalizi–Newman power-law MLE with x_min chosen to minimize the KS distance between empirical and fitted CDF restricted to s ≥ x_min (α_P = 1 + n/Σ_i log(s_i/x_min)). This is the headline estimator.
- Robustness estimators, reported alongside: α_H Hill with plateau selection (sweep k∈[10, d/2], pick the k where α_H(k) is flattest); α_RF rank–frequency OLS slope of log s_i vs log i over top-k tail (k = min(⌈0.3d⌉, 200)).
- Tail index CI: percentile bootstrap (B=1000) over seeds×layers within a module type, and per-module bootstrap over SVD-noise-free resamples (singular values themselves), BCa or percentile.
- A tail is called heavy if estimated α ∈ (0, ~3) with lower confidence bound < ~2 (qualitative sanity check; the formal verdict uses the comparability rule, not an absolute heavy-ness threshold).

2.3 Effective rank measures (same SVD):
- Participation ratio PR = (Σ s_i)² / Σ s_i².
- Variance-threshold rank r_τ = smallest r with (Σ_{i≤r} s_i²)/(Σ s_i²) ≥ τ, τ ∈ {0.9, 0.99}; report normalized r_τ/d so values are comparable across 768×768 and 768×2048 modules.

2.4 "Comparable" — pre-registered decision rule (primary, set before running):
For each module m we pair the same-seed, same-module descriptors across arms.
(i) Effective-rank ratio: ρ_m = r(m; BAdam)/r(m; Adam) (for r = r_0.9/d; also report PR-ratio). Call m rank-comparable iff ρ_m ∈ [0.80, 1.25] (equal on log-scale to ±log 1.25 ≈ ±0.223).
(ii) Tail comparability: call m tail-comparable iff the 95% bootstrap CIs of α_P(BAdam) and α_P(Adam) for m overlap.
Global answer (mechanical):
- YES: (A) median over m of ρ_m ∈ [0.80, 1.25]; AND (B) ≥ 80% of modules rank-comparable; AND (C) ≥ 80% of modules tail-comparable.
- NO: any of (A)/(B)/(C) fails; in that case also report which of the three conditions failed and by how much.
Report all three conditions explicitly; the single-word verdict follows from the rule. Per-module-type medians, |Δα| distribution, and spiked-component counts (2.6/4) are reported as diagnostics, not as verdict inputs. Equivalence backup: TOST-style two-one-sided bounds on log ρ with ±log(1.25), reported per module type as descriptive p-values (modules are not independent i.i.d. samples, so this is corroborating only).

2.5 Interpretation mapping: the research question's target "comparable" is exactly the conjunction in 2.4. A "sí" is the mechanical output of the rule; a "no" is reported with the failing component. No experiment is claimed to have produced either outcome here.

2.6 Numerical-noise handling (for possibly small BAdam perturbations): For each module, estimate the noise-floor singular values via the Marc̆enko–Pastur bulk: fit the MP law to the small-singular-value bulk using the module's aspect ratio and an empirical noise variance; σ_edge = MP bulk edge. Count #spiked components above σ_edge. If #spiked < 5 for a module, mark its α and r_τ as low-confidence: EXCLUDE it from statistics (B) and (C) of the verdict but list it in an appendix table with its scale ‖ΔW‖_F. Additionally verify SVD stability by recomputing the largest ~50 singular values with double-reorthogonalized SVD and comparing to dense SVD (a sanity check, since some SVD packs under-estimate small singular values for thin matrices).

# 3 Controls and comparison structure

3.1 Fixed across arms (all runs): identical W_0 checkpoint (same random init from fixed seed s0, deep-copied into every arm; if a pretrained checkpoint were available it would be the same object for all arms), same tokenizer and fixed shuffled data order (deterministic RNG), same batches, same optimizer hyperparameters (AdamW: lr=2e-5, β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=1e-8, weight_decay=0.0 primary / 0.01 robustness sweep), same cosine schedule with 5% warmup over the SAME global step count T, same seq_len/batch/epochs, same validation split and metric (per-token cross-entropy). The only difference across arms is the optimizer's block structure.

3.2 Randomness: weights seeded at s0 and identical across all arms; shuffle seed fixed; 5 experiment seeds {0,1,2,3,4} reproduce data-shuffle/tokenizer/batch randomness across arms (each seed runs ALL arms, giving paired same-seed observations). All CIs pooled over seeds and layers for type-level, and per-same-seed for module-level pairing.

3.3 Adam vs BAdam grid (primary convention): arms = {Adam} ∪ {BAdam, K∈{2,4,12}} × seeds {0..4} = 20 runs. BAdam blocks: contiguous layer groups that never split a layer: K=2 → layers {0-5},{6-11}; K=4 → {0-2},{3-5},{6-8},{9-11}; K=12 → one block per layer; blocks cyclically activated (one active block per global step using that block's Adam states; others frozen); per-layer modules always stay together.

3.4 Primary convention — EQUAL FORWARD PASSES: T_Adam = T_Badam = T=733 global steps for all arms (same epochs, same schedule object over same global indices). Implication: each Adam module gets n_m ≈ 733 active solver steps; each BAdam module gets n_m ≈ ⌊733/K⌋ (≈366 for K=2, 183 for K=4, 61 for K=12). This directly matches the BAdam paper's evaluation protocol (same data passes), and since the verdict metrics are scale-invariant, the expected fewer-active-step per-module effect is isolated as the "block structure effect" rather than a magnitude confound.
3.5 Secondary convention — EQUAL PER-BLOCK ACTIVE STEPS (robustness): run BAdam for K·T global steps so every module receives n_m ≈ T ≈ 733 active steps, i.e., the same number of applied Adam increments per module as in the Adam arm. This requires K× more forward passes and a K× longer schedule; we also run a "per-cycle LR restart" variant of the same schedule to decorrelate total-schedule-length from per-block update count. Report both primary and secondary verdicts; a conclusion is called stable iff primary and secondary agree under both conventions and under wd∈{0,0.01}.

# 4 Analysis plan

4.1 Per-run extraction: for every module m: ΔW_m, n_m, ‖ΔW_m‖_F; SVD → {α_P, α_H, α_RF, their CIs}, {PR, r_0.9/d, r_0.99/d}, #spiked (MP bulk edge), scale ‖ΔW_m‖_F.
4.2 Type-level table (the main deliverable): rows = module type ∈ {q, k, v, o, up, gate, down}; columns = arm (Adam, BAdam K=2/4/12) × descriptor: α_P (median, 95% bootstrap CI over layers & seeds), α_H, α_RF, PR, r_0.9/d, r_0.99/d, ‖ΔW‖_F, plus paired ρ_m and Δα = α_B − α_A with CI, and #spiked. Same layout for primary and secondary conventions.
4.3 Layer-depth curves: for each arm, r_0.9/d(ℓ) and α_P(ℓ) vs layer ℓ∈0..11 (median and CI band over seeds), Adam and BAdam(K=4) overlaid; other K in appendix.
4.4 Pairwise statistics: histogram/empirical-CDF of ρ_m and of |Δα| across the 84 modules; per-type TOST-equivalence summary; report the fraction failing each verdict condition.
4.5 Sensitivity of the verdict: (i) re-fit α_P across x_min percentile choices (e.g., x_min ∈ 10th..90th percentile of tail) and recompute condition (C); (ii) r_τ with τ∈{0.5, 0.9, 0.99}; (iii) wd∈{0, 0.01}; (iv) primary vs secondary convention; (v) #spiked threshold 3 vs 5. The verdict is reported as robust to (i)–(v) or the specific sensitive axis is named.
4.6 Appendix: low-confidence modules (per 2.6), embedding/lm_head spectral appendix, per-seed raw tables.

# 5 Feasibility
- Main cost is the finetuning, not the SVD. ~110M-param forward/backward at seq=256: ≈ 8–16 GFLOP/step; 733 steps/run → ~1e13–1.2e13 FLOP/run. On 224 CPU cores with a vectorized CPU torch build, estimate ≈0.5–2 h/run; primary grid 20 runs fully parallelizable → ≈10–40 CPU-core-hours total (a few hours wall-clock at this core count). Secondary grid (K·T with T=733) ≈ 3× more steps aggregate.
- SVD per module is negligible: largest matrix 768×2048 → O(768²·2048) ≈ 1.2 GFLOP ≈ <1 s on CPU; 84 modules + appendix ≈ <2 min/run. Memory: model ~110M params ≈ 0.5 GB fp32; block-wise optimizer states ≈ full-Adam states only for the active block ≈ small footprint.
- Environment note: this sandbox has Python 3.14.4 but NO numpy/torch/transformers installed and network is disabled, so a real run REQUIRES installing dependencies (torch, transformers or a minimal custom LLaMA forward/backward in pure torch/numpy) and providing the local corpus file — explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this design task. No results are claimed; this is a design-only deliverable.

# 6 Uncertainties and how they are mitigated/reported
- U1 — α sensitivity to tail selection (x_min/k). Mitigations: primary = CSN x_min via KS; report α_H plateau and α_RF; run the x_min sweep (4.5i) and state whether the verdict is stable.
- U2 — Definition of "equality" Adam vs BAdam (equal epochs vs equal per-block steps). Mitigations: pre-register BOTH conventions (primary=equal forward passes per BAdam paper protocol; secondary=equal per-block active steps); report both; conclusion "stable iff" both agree.
- U3 — Scaling from BAdam's paper conventions (LLaMA-2-7B layer-range blocks) to our K∈{2,4,12} layer-group blocks. Mitigations: contiguous layer groups not splitting layers mirror the paper's block structure; K sweep covers coarse→per-layer granularity; clearly labeled as a scale-down analog, not a replication.
- U4 — Numerical noise for very small ΔW (SVD under-estimates tiny singular values; BAdam may yield smaller per-module displacement). Mitigations: MP bulk-edge spiked-component counting, low-confidence module flagging/exclusion, dense-SVD vs reorthogonalized-SVD sanity check, and scale-free metrics (α, PR, r/d) that do not conflate magnitude with shape.
- U5 — Module non-independence (84 modules share layers/seeds) makes classic hypothesis tests optimistic. Mitigations: verdict uses medians & CI overlap, not i.i.d. assumptions; TOST reported as descriptive only; pairing is same-seed same-module.
- U6 — Corpus/model are not BAdam's original LLaMA-7B/instruction data; the design targets structural (shape) comparability which is scale-invariant, and any limitation to generalizing beyond our 110M/1M-token setup is stated as such.
- Assumption list (fixed requirements vs choices): fixed = answer the yes/no question with pre-registered rules; design-only; CPU budget constraints (≤~125M model, small token budget). Choices (can be revised) = tiny-LLaMA-110M, Wiki-2-style 1M-token slice, K∈{2,4,12}, T=733, 5 seeds, thresholds ρ∈[0.8,1.25]/80% overlap, CSN α_P as primary tail estimator.
